## What if we want to compare many treatments?

Our motivating example: Cipriani _et al._, _Comparative efficacy and acceptability of antimanic drugs in acute mania: a multiple-treatments meta-analysis_ (2011), the Lancet

- Influential paper (600+ citations)
- Meta-analysis experts
- Realistic scope
- Highlights typical outputs
- ...but also challenges

## Network meta-analysis 

- Loosely: any meta-analysis with more than two comparators
- Direct comparisons, many treatments (studies with 2+ arms)
- Indirect comparisons: "traversing the graph"
- Also known as ITC, MTC

- MA: pairwise or direct
- NMA: Multi-arm studies, pairwise studies with more than 2 treatments

## Acceptability of NMA

- "New kid on the block": much younger than MA
- See e.g. ["Is network meta-analysis as valid as standard pairwise meta-analysis?" (2013)](https://bmcmedicine.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1741-7015-11-159)
- Most widely developed/promoted in health technology assessment, e.g. NICE DSU

Let's draw a simple example.


## Additional assumptions

- Joint randomisability ("you'd put them in the same study")
- Transitivity (same populations/effect modifiers)
- Consistency ("take any path in the graph")

Transitivity is hard to test for. Consistency a bit easier, but low power.

If not assuming FE: 

- Heterogeneity (same or different across each pairwise comparison?)
- Within trial correlations

## NMA outputs

Revisit Cipriani et al. paper

- Pairwise comparison matrix
- Forest plots
- Rankograms

## Implementation

- MA has simple Bayesian and frequentist implementations
- Situation a bit more complicated than in the case of MA.
- Frequentist in R: `netmeta` (good, mature software)
- But many regulators (rightly) prefer Bayesian methods
- Bayesian in R: `gemtc` (mature, but slightly less user-friendly)

Some situations require bespoke models.


## More complicated situations

- Reminder: (in multi-arm studies) we typically meta-analyse SMD, OR, RR, HR
- But you can write _any_ parameteric model in Bayesian inference
- ...and analyse it hierarchically
- Consider a model of survival or a PKPD model
- ...just need data to infer these parameters
- Individual level data often inferred from summary-level data
- Blurry line between meta-analysis and hierarchical modeling

In pharma world this is referred by some as [model-based meta-analysis](https://www.certara.com/services/model-based-meta-analysis/)

-----

Worked example in WinBUGS ([link](https://github.com/certara/survivalnma/blob/master/inst/bugs_models/bugs_model_exponential.txt)): 

\tiny


```
Model{
	for (i in 1:N){ # N=number of data points in dataset
		#likelihood
		r[i]~ dbin(p[i],n[i])
		p[i]<-1-exp(-h[i]*dt[i])

		log(h[i])<-nu[i] + log(time[i])*theta[i]
		nu[i]<-mu[s[i]]+delta[s[i]]*(1-equals(t[i],b[i]))
		theta[i]<-0
		}

	for(k in 1 :NS){ # NS=number of studies in dataset
		delta[k] <- md[k]
		md[k]<-d[ts[k]]-d[bs[k]]
	}

	# priors
		d[1]<-0
	for(j in 2 :NT){ # NT=number of treatments
		d[j] ~ dnorm(mean[1],prec2[1,1])
	}
	for(k in 1 :NS){
		mu[k] ~ dnorm(mean[1],prec2[1,1])
	}
}
```



## A few resources that recap NMA for you

- Nice online book by Matthais Harrier:
    - Intro to [frequentist NMA](https://bookdown.org/MathiasHarrer/Doing_Meta_Analysis_in_R/netwma.html)
    - Intro to [Bayesian NMA (gemtc)](https://bookdown.org/MathiasHarrer/Doing_Meta_Analysis_in_R/bayesian-ma.html)
- Big textbook: [Dias et al. (2018)](https://www.wiley.com/en-es/Network+Meta+Analysis+for+Decision+Making-p-9781118647509)
- [Cipriani et al. (2011)](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(11)60873-8/fulltext)
- [NICE DSU technical support document on Bayesian NMA](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK310366/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK310366.pdf): directly relevant to the regulator, oldie but goodie
    - Also see subsequent documents (vol 3-4; this is vol. 2)
- [NMA of parametric survival curves (Ouwens paper)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26061470/)
    - [survivalnma](https://github.com/certara/survivalnma) package
